prompt_md: A 100 m rail is pinned at both ends. On a hot day it grows 2 cm and buckles up into a sharp peak at its middle, as two straight halves. How high is the peak, in cm?
prompt_short: 100 m rail grows 2 cm and buckles into a peak. Height of the peak?
hint_md: Each half is a 50.01 m hypotenuse over a 50 m base.
explain_intuition_md: Two centimetres of extra length feels like it should lift the rail by a centimetre or so. But a slightly longer hypotenuse over a long base stands surprisingly tall: the height grows with the square root of the stretch.
